From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
  SPA-N-003: General claims time limit

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

## Headline points

1. **The Seller's cover note conflicts with its own Disclosure Letter.**
   - Bluefen is described as "addressed", but DL §2 says no consent has been delivered.
   - The export incident is described as "not expected to be material", but DL §6 says the investigation is preliminary and scope is unknown.
   - Riverlark is to be released "following Completion", but DL §3 says the facility is unpaid and undischarged.

   We should rely on the Disclosure Letter's admissions and reject the cover note's characterisations.

2. **The Seller wants one limitation regime for everything.** The combined effect of 12.8, 20.5, the "all Claims" wording and the fundamental warranties being capped at AUD 4.8m would cap fraud, title, tax and specific indemnities at 20% of price. This is the most important structural point to resist.

3. **About AUD 3.95m of known leakage or exposure is not dealt with in the price mechanics.** This covers Riverlark (AUD 3.2m), the bonuses (AUD 420k plus on-costs) and Sandbar (AUD 330k). These should be handled through the funds flow and specific indemnities, not left to capped warranty claims.

---

## Issue-by-issue

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Liability for general warranty claims is capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer wants:** A cap of 35–50% of price (AUD 8.4m–12m) for general warranties. The cap must apply *only* to general warranties, with the full price as the cap for fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities. If warranty and indemnity insurance is used, structure the Seller's retention and cap around the policy.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 50% and accept no less than about 30%. **Reason:** 20% is at the low end for a business with a 30% customer-concentration risk, an open IP chain and a live privacy incident.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis of AUD 25k. Basket of AUD 250k, operating as a deductible (only the excess is recoverable).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - De minimis of AUD 10–15k, with related or recurring claims aggregated for testing purposes.
  - Basket of about AUD 120k (0.5%).
  - A **tipping** basket, so the full amount is recoverable once the threshold is crossed.
  - No thresholds applying to fundamental, tax or specific-indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the deductible and counter as above. **Reason:** A deductible at 1% of price permanently loses the Buyer AUD 250k of real loss, and without aggregation related claims could each fall under the de minimis.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion for general claims. Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - 24 months for general warranties, so the period covers two full audit cycles.
  - Tax claims: the ATO amendment period plus 6 months, or a minimum of 5–7 years.
  - Title and capacity: 7 years or the statutory limitation period.
  - Specific indemnities: their own periods, for example the privacy indemnity runs until regulatory matters close plus 12 months.
  - Reverse the default. Each category should have its *own* stated period, and nothing should be inherited by default.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" wording. **Reason:** That default quietly cuts tax, title and indemnity claims down to 18 months.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental and title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties take the same cap and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Title, capacity, authority and solvency warranties capped at 100% of price, with no thresholds, a 7-year or statutory period, and no disclosure against them.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright. **Reason:** If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing. Recovery capped at AUD 4.8m is not "simplicity", it is a transfer of 80% of the core risk.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Silent on fraud. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature", which on its face includes fraud.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - An express carve-out stating that no limitation, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provision applies to fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers, agents or Company management.
  - An express carve-out preserving claims for misleading or deceptive conduct under s 18 of the Australian Consumer Law (CCA Sch 2), to the extent they cannot lawfully be excluded.
- **Recommendation:** Insert the express carve-out. This is non-negotiable. **Reason:** Courts are unlikely to let a party exclude liability for its own fraud, but an "of any nature" drafting position invites argument, and the carve-out should be explicit.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (as at 22 Sep 2026), the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records (DL §§1.1–1.2), plus a non-admission clause (§1.4).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Only *specific* disclosures in the Disclosure Letter count, and only to the extent they are **fairly disclosed** with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter.
  - No general disclosure of the data room or public records.
  - No disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax or specific indemnities.
  - Disclosure does not qualify specific indemnities.
  - A frozen, indexed data room copy (USB or archive) attached for evidence only.
- **Recommendation:** Delete §§1.1–1.2 or strictly limit them. Accept §1.4 only if it is made clear that it does not dilute the factual disclosures. **Reason:** General disclosure of the data room effectively converts the warranties into the Buyer's own diligence risk.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the clause, or replace it with a pro-Buyer position: the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge, except matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter. If any knowledge qualifier survives, limit it to the *actual* knowledge of named deal-team individuals, exclude advisers, and exclude constructive knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert a "no effect of investigation" clause. **Reason:** Combined with general disclosure, imputed and constructive knowledge of advisers could defeat almost any claim.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Says the consent is "addressed". The Seller will use reasonable endeavours, and the condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Facts (DL §2):** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. Change-of-control consent is required under cl 11.2, subject to conditions in cl 11.3. **No consent and no evidence that the conditions are satisfied** has been provided.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A condition precedent of written, *unconditional* consent from Bluefen (or consent on terms acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably), covering satisfaction or waiver of the cl 11.3 conditions.
  - No adverse amendment to the contract, with the waiver right sitting with the Buyer only.
  - A "best/all reasonable endeavours" standard on the Seller.
  - A sunset date with a Buyer termination right.
  - Consider a price adjustment or earn-out if Bluefen terminates or renegotiates within 12 months.
- **Recommendation:** Make this a hard Buyer-waivable condition. Do not accept "satisfied on delivery of consent" unless the cl 11.3 conditions are also covered. **Reason:** Losing about 30% of revenue would fundamentally impair value, and consent with unsatisfied conditions is not real protection.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release is "to be provided following Completion".
- **Facts (DL §3):** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. Change of control under cl 8.1 likely triggers default or prepayment. The facility has not been repaid and there is no discharge of security.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Repayment **at Completion** out of the price, as Debt deducted under the debt-free/cash-free mechanism.
  - A payout letter delivered before Completion.
  - Executed deed of release and discharge, PPSR financing-change statements and releases of any guarantees, all delivered at Completion as a deliverable.
  - A full indemnity for any residual facility amounts (break costs, default interest).
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release and make it a Completion deliverable paid through the funds flow. **Reason:** Otherwise the Buyer takes a AUD 3.2m secured, potentially defaulted facility in a company it now owns, on an unsecured promise from the Seller.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The AUD 420k of Completion bonuses (DD-005) is "a matter for the Seller" and is not shown in the funds flow.
- **Facts (DL §5):** The bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment. Payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs have not been addressed.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The bonuses *plus all on-costs* (PAYG withholding, super guarantee where applicable, NSW payroll tax, workers' compensation) treated as Debt or transaction costs and deducted from the price.
  - Paid through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded from the deduction.
  - An indemnity for any shortfall or later-crystallising amounts.
- **Recommendation:** Itemise them in the funds flow as a price deduction. **Reason:** These are Company liabilities triggered by the Seller's sale. If they are left out of the funds flow, the Buyer pays them on top of AUD 24m.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is said to be "adequate".
- **Facts (DL §4):** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. AUD 180k is shown as open (DD-010). There is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Before Completion:** payment of the AUD 180k (Seller cost, or treated as Debt), plus an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, with moral rights consents where relevant. Make these a condition or Completion deliverable.
  - **Fallback:** a specific indemnity covering *all* loss from any defect in the Company's title to the SOW3 materials. This should include third-party claims, re-development cost and loss of use, and should be uncapped or capped at price, with no thresholds and outside the general regime.
  - An IP title warranty treated as a fundamental-style warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Require a confirmatory assignment at Completion. Do not accept a payment-only indemnity. **Reason:** The risk is not the AUD 180k fee but that the Company may not own core product IP.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** Calls it a "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material".
- **Facts (DL §6):** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) may be affected. Access, scope and notification obligations are all unknown, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A pre-Completion covenant that the Seller completes the investigation, with Buyer access and consultation rights.
  - An assessment under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act 1988, Part IIIC), within the 30-day assessment window, with the Buyer reviewing any notification to the OAIC or individuals.
  - Contract-level notifications to affected customers checked, since Bluefen and other customer DPAs may have shorter windows.
  - A **specific indemnity**, outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure, for regulatory penalties, investigation and remediation costs, customer claims and credits, and notification costs.
  - Consider a retention or escrow amount.
  - A specific data-protection warranty brought down at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Require a specific indemnity plus investigation covenants. Reject the "not material" characterisation. **Reason:** The Seller's own letter says the scope is unknown and has not been assessed, so materiality cannot yet be asserted.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** The three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k in total) are "ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Facts (DL §8):** The renewals are related, and DD-008 and DD-011 must be "read together for timing/scope". The letter does not say whether each one is unavoidable, terminable or accrued, or whether it is actually in the ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Diligence on the timing of the renewals relative to signing and the sale process, whether they are on arm's-length terms, any Seller-related party involvement, and termination rights.
  - Any amount committed but unaccrued for pre-Completion periods treated as Debt or a working-capital liability.
  - A conduct-of-business covenant that prohibits further renewals or commitments above about AUD 50k without Buyer consent.
  - The three renewals treated as one matter for de minimis and basket purposes.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept an "ordinary course" label without evidence. Price-adjust or indemnify if the renewals are not genuine. **Reason:** Three linked renewals pushed through during a sale process look like potential leakage, and "read together" signals they may be one AUD 330k commitment.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single regime: the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Separate, express regimes for each category:

| Category | Cap | Thresholds | Time limit | Disclosure applies? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| General warranties | 35–50% | De minimis and tipping basket | 24 months | Specific, fair disclosure only |
| Fundamental (title/capacity) | 100% | None | 7 years | No |
| Tax warranties and indemnity | 100% | None | ATO period + 6 months | No |
| Specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, Riverlark, bonuses) | 100% or uncapped | None | Matter-specific | No |
| Fraud / wilful concealment | Unlimited | None | Statutory | No |

  Non-reliance should be limited to pre-contract statements not repeated in the SPA, and should not affect fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Restructure clause 12 by category. **Reason:** The single-regime drafting is the mechanism through which all the other protections are diluted.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012.
- **Facts (DL §10):** The letter expressly says it only identifies the source relied on and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Independent verification through current ASIC company extracts and the historical share issue and transfer chain (Forms 484 and similar).
  - The constitution and any shareholders' agreement, checking pre-emption rights, options, convertible notes and ESOP.
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company.
  - Original share certificates, stamped transfers and board minutes approving the issues.
  - Completion deliverables: a signed transfer form, share certificates, a waiver of pre-emption rights and releases of any security over the shares.
  - Uncapped title warranties: legal and beneficial owner, free of Encumbrances, no options or rights to issue shares.
- **Recommendation:** Complete our own verification and keep title warranties fundamental and uncapped. **Reason:** A register maintained by the company itself is not proof of unencumbered beneficial title, and the Seller has carefully avoided saying it is.

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller:** Considers the tax and IP positions "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** a standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax on the bonuses and any GST or income tax adjustments. It should be capped at price, run for the ATO amendment period plus 6 months, have no thresholds and not be subject to disclosure. Add conduct-of-claims and return-preparation mechanics.
  - **IP:** expanded IP warranties covering ownership, valid assignments from all employees and contractors (including Ironquay), no infringement, open-source compliance and source-code control. These should have a 36-month period and sit at least under a higher sub-cap.
- **Recommendation:** Treat both as **open**, not settled. Table a tax indemnity and an IP schedule in our mark-up. **Reason:** Nothing has been agreed. Putting tax and IP under an 18-month, 20%-capped, data-room-disclosed regime would leave the Buyer's most likely post-Completion exposures largely uncovered.

---

## Suggested next steps
1. **Reply to the Seller's counsel:** note the inconsistencies between the cover note and the Disclosure Letter (Bluefen, Riverlark, DD-006) and confirm that the Buyer relies on the Disclosure Letter as written.
2. **Mark up the SPA:**
   - Restructure clause 12 by category.
   - Add a fraud carve-out.
   - Delete or replace clause 8.3.
   - Add the Bluefen condition precedent.
   - Add Completion deliverables for Riverlark and Ironquay.
   - Add the bonus, on-cost and Sandbar treatment to the debt definitions and funds flow.
   - Add specific indemnities for privacy, Ironquay and tax.
3. **Complete diligence:** finish title verification, review the Bluefen cl 11.3 conditions, assess the DD-006 incident with privacy counsel, and look into the Sandbar renewals.
4. **Consider W&I insurance:** if it is being considered, line up the underwriter now. Known matters (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses) will be excluded from cover and must be dealt with through specific indemnities and price.

The market ranges above are indicative for an Australian mid-market share sale and should be confirmed against the deal team's commercial priorities and any W&I terms.

- **Buyer wants:** Delete the clause, or replace it with a pro-Buyer position: the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge, except matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter. If any knowledge qualifier survives, limit it to the *actual* knowledge of named deal-team individuals, exclude advisers, and exclude constructive knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert a "no effect of investigation" clause. **Reason:** Combined with general disclosure, imputed and constructive knowledge of advisers could defeat almost any claim.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Says the consent is "addressed". The Seller will use reasonable endeavours, and the condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Facts (DL §2):** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. Change-of-control consent is required under cl 11.2, subject to conditions in cl 11.3. **No consent and no evidence that the conditions are satisfied** has been provided.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A condition precedent of written, *unconditional* consent from Bluefen (or consent on terms acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably), covering satisfaction or waiver of the cl 11.3 conditions.
  - No adverse amendment to the contract, with the waiver right sitting with the Buyer only.
  - A "best/all reasonable endeavours" standard on the Seller.
  - A sunset date with a Buyer termination right.
  - Consider a price adjustment or earn-out if Bluefen terminates or renegotiates within 12 months.
- **Recommendation:** Make this a hard Buyer-waivable condition. Do not accept "satisfied on delivery of consent" unless the cl 11.3 conditions are also covered. **Reason:** Losing about 30% of revenue would fundamentally impair value, and consent with unsatisfied conditions is not real protection.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release is "to be provided following Completion".
- **Facts (DL §3):** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. Change of control under cl 8.1 likely triggers default or prepayment. The facility has not been repaid and there is no discharge of security.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Repayment **at Completion** out of the price, as Debt deducted under the debt-free/cash-free mechanism.
  - A payout letter delivered before Completion.
  - Executed deed of release and discharge, PPSR financing-change statements and releases of any guarantees, all delivered at Completion as a deliverable.
  - A full indemnity for any residual facility amounts (break costs, default interest).
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release and make it a Completion deliverable paid through the funds flow. **Reason:** Otherwise the Buyer takes a AUD 3.2m secured, potentially defaulted facility in a company it now owns, on an unsecured promise from the Seller.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The AUD 420k of Completion bonuses (DD-005) is "a matter for the Seller" and is not shown in the funds flow.
- **Facts (DL §5):** The bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment. Payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs have not been addressed.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The bonuses *plus all on-costs* (PAYG withholding, super guarantee where applicable, NSW payroll tax, workers' compensation) treated as Debt or transaction costs and deducted from the price.
  - Paid through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded from the deduction.
  - An indemnity for any shortfall or later-crystallising amounts.
- **Recommendation:** Itemise them in the funds flow as a price deduction. **Reason:** These are Company liabilities triggered by the Seller's sale. If they are left out of the funds flow, the Buyer pays them on top of AUD 24m.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is said to be "adequate".
- **Facts (DL §4):** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. AUD 180k is shown as open (DD-010). There is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Before Completion:** payment of the AUD 180k (Seller cost, or treated as Debt), plus an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, with moral rights consents where relevant. Make these a condition or Completion deliverable.
  - **Fallback:** a specific indemnity covering *all* loss from any defect in the Company's title to the SOW3 materials. This should include third-party claims, re-development cost and loss of use, and should be uncapped or capped at price, with no thresholds and outside the general regime.
  - An IP title warranty treated as a fundamental-style warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Require a confirmatory assignment at Completion. Do not accept a payment-only indemnity. **Reason:** The risk is not the AUD 180k fee but that the Company may not own core product IP.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** Calls it a "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material".
- **Facts (DL §6):** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) may be affected. Access, scope and notification obligations are all unknown, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A pre-Completion covenant that the Seller completes the investigation, with Buyer access and consultation rights.
  - An assessment under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act 1988, Part IIIC), within the 30-day assessment window, with the Buyer reviewing any notification to the OAIC or individuals.
  - Contract-level notifications to affected customers checked, since Bluefen and other customer DPAs may have shorter windows.
  - A **specific indemnity**, outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure, for regulatory penalties, investigation and remediation costs, customer claims and credits, and notification costs.
  - Consider a retention or escrow amount.
  - A specific data-protection warranty brought down at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Require a specific indemnity plus investigation covenants. Reject the "not material" characterisation. **Reason:** The Seller's own letter says the scope is unknown and has not been assessed, so materiality cannot yet be asserted.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** The three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k in total) are "ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Facts (DL §8):** The renewals are related, and DD-008 and DD-011 must be "read together for timing/scope". The letter does not say whether each one is unavoidable, terminable or accrued, or whether it is actually in the ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Diligence on the timing of the renewals relative to signing and the sale process, whether they are on arm's-length terms, any Seller-related party involvement, and termination rights.
  - Any amount committed but unaccrued for pre-Completion periods treated as Debt or a working-capital liability.
  - A conduct-of-business covenant that prohibits further renewals or commitments above about AUD 50k without Buyer consent.
  - The three renewals treated as one matter for de minimis and basket purposes.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept an "ordinary course" label without evidence. Price-adjust or indemnify if the renewals are not genuine. **Reason:** Three linked renewals pushed through during a sale process look like potential leakage, and "read together" signals they may be one AUD 330k commitment.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single regime: the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Separate, express regimes for each category:

| Category | Cap | Thresholds | Time limit | Disclosure applies? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| General warranties | 35–50% | De minimis and tipping basket | 24 months | Specific, fair disclosure only |
| Fundamental (title/capacity) | 100% | None | 7 years | No |
| Tax warranties and indemnity | 100% | None | ATO period + 6 months | No |
| Specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, Riverlark, bonuses) | 100% or uncapped | None | Matter-specific | No |
| Fraud / wilful concealment | Unlimited | None | Statutory | No |

  Non-reliance should be limited to pre-contract statements not repeated in the SPA, and should not affect fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Restructure clause 12 by category. **Reason:** The single-regime drafting is the mechanism through which all the other protections are diluted.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012.
- **Facts (DL §10):** The letter expressly says it only identifies the source relied on and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Independent verification through current ASIC company extracts and the historical share issue and transfer chain (Forms 484 and similar).
  - The constitution and any shareholders' agreement, checking pre-emption rights, options, convertible notes and ESOP.
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company.
  - Original share certificates, stamped transfers and board minutes approving the issues.
  - Completion deliverables: a signed transfer form, share certificates, a waiver of pre-emption rights and releases of any security over the shares.
  - Uncapped title warranties: legal and beneficial owner, free of Encumbrances, no options or rights to issue shares.
- **Recommendation:** Complete our own verification and keep title warranties fundamental and uncapped. **Reason:** A register maintained by the company itself is not proof of unencumbered beneficial title, and the Seller has carefully avoided saying it is.

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller:** Considers the tax and IP positions "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** a standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax on the bonuses and any GST or income tax adjustments. It should be capped at price, run for the ATO amendment period plus 6 months, have no thresholds and not be subject to disclosure. Add conduct-of-claims and return-preparation mechanics.
  - **IP:** expanded IP warranties covering ownership, valid assignments from all employees and contractors (including Ironquay), no infringement, open-source compliance and source-code control. These should have a 36-month period and sit at least under a higher sub-cap.
- **Recommendation:** Treat both as **open**, not settled. Table a tax indemnity and an IP schedule in our mark-up. **Reason:** Nothing has been agreed. Putting tax and IP under an 18-month, 20%-capped, data-room-disclosed regime would leave the Buyer's most likely post-Completion exposures largely uncovered.
